domains.backend: Request handling, APIs, databases, queues, caching.
domains.data: Transformation, parsing, serialization, pipelines, file I/O.
domains.ml: Model loading, inference, embeddings, training utilities.
domains.infra: Deployment, config management, logging, monitoring, health checks.
domains.universal: Pure utilities with no domain dependency (string ops, retry, math, date handling). If a widget could reasonably belong to two domains, it belongs here.
domains.modeling: Parametric and generative representations of physical or visual things — 3D geometry, surfaces, shapes, simulations. Widgets produce artifacts (STL, mesh, image) rather than running as services.
domains.rtl: Register-transfer level hardware design — synthesizable digital logic modules. Widgets are parameterized RTL modules in SystemVerilog (.sv) that compile and simulate cleanly. No vendor primitives, no simulation-only constructs in src/.
domains.devops: Infrastructure-as-code, deployment, and operational tooling. Widgets are reusable cloud/on-prem patterns (Terraform modules, IAM policies, network primitives, deployment topologies) whose value compounds as more consumers harden them. Validation is shape-only: declarations parse and references resolve. Runtime behavior is the consumer's responsibility.

general_notes: Single responsibility - one widget does one thing. No global state. No project-specific code, hardcoded paths, credentials, or environment-specific values. Expose variation points as constructor parameters or function arguments - no hardcoded thresholds, colors, sizes, or behavior flags. URLs and endpoints belong in examples as demonstration data, not in src/ - if a widget needs a URL to operate, it must be a parameter the caller provides. All dependencies must be declared in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies. Widgets cannot depend on other widgets - they must be fully self-contained. If you need logic from another widget, copy it into src/ directly. Examples must run and exit cleanly with no user input, no network calls, and no external services or API keys - use fake/hardcoded data. The widget's own declared dependencies are fine and will be installed by the validator before the example runs. Do not modify library_notes - it is managed by Cartograph and will be restored on checkin.

language_notes.python: No project-specific names, identifiers, or terminology anywhere in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic names like 'user', 'item', 'value', 'example_org'. A test that references your project's real entity names is contaminated. Use pytest for all tests - no unittest. Type hints required on all public functions. No __init__.py in tests/. No if __name__ == '__main__' blocks in src/ files. Imports ordered: stdlib, third-party, local. ML domain: framework-free (numpy, scikit-learn, plain Python) and API-based inference (HTTP calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace Inference API) work everywhere. Heavy optional frameworks must be pre-installed - Cartograph will not auto-install them. Declare dependencies in widget.json normally; consumers must also have them installed to validate.
language_notes.javascript: No project-specific names, identifiers, or terminology anywhere in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic names like 'user', 'item', 'value', 'example.com'. A test that references your project's real entity names or domain is contaminated. Use vitest for all tests. Include a vitest config and a coverage provider (@vitest/coverage-v8 or @vitest/coverage-istanbul) in devDependencies - the validator enforces 80% coverage via CLI flags but does not inject test configuration. No console.log() in src/ files. Use named exports, not default exports. Test filename must match src filename exactly. Only test/expect/describe/vi are global - all other imports must be explicit. Plain JS: files use .js, examples run with node and exit cleanly. Frontend (DOM) testing: add 'happy-dom' to devDependencies and set environment: 'happy-dom' in your vitest config - the scaffold does this automatically for frontend widgets. Canvas/WebGL testing: add '@vitest/browser' and 'playwright' to devDependencies and configure the browser provider in your vitest config - Playwright must be installed on the system (run 'npx playwright install chromium'). React is not scaffolded by default. To use React: add react and react-dom to widget.json tech_stack.dependencies and package.json dependencies; rename files to .jsx; add @vitejs/plugin-react, @testing-library/react, and jsdom to package.json devDependencies; configure your vitest config with the react plugin and jsdom environment. Examples with a non-.js extension (.jsx, .ts, .tsx) run via `npx tsx` - no bundler step. Test environment is entirely your vitest config's responsibility - Cartograph does not inject React dev-deps. Components must be PascalCase .jsx, hooks camelCase .js starting with 'use'. Components must render cleanly via react-dom/server renderToString with no browser APIs (window, document, localStorage) in the initial render path. Usage hints: you may optionally include examples/usage_hint.* with real integration code that requires a browser or app context. These are not executed by Cartograph.
language_notes.openscad: No project-specific names, part numbers, or assembly identifiers in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic descriptive names. Use module for all reusable geometry — never write top-level statements outside a module in src/, including calls to your own modules (no preview instantiations). All parameters must have defaults so the module renders on its own. Every src/*.scad file must declare a coordinate frame at the top using one or more // COORDINATES (cartesian|cylindrical|spherical): blocks. At least one block must be fully filled in (no placeholders) with all required fields. Cartesian requires Origin, +X, +Y, +Z. Cylindrical requires Axis, Origin, theta. Spherical requires Origin, theta, phi. Right-hand rule is assumed across all three systems. Multiple frames are allowed when a part is genuinely dual (e.g. a gear that's both cylindrical-by-rotation and cartesian-by-mounting); delete frames you don't use. All dimensions are millimeters and angles are degrees unless explicitly noted in a parameter's unit comment. Tests are .scad files that call your module with different parameters — each must render to a non-empty STL without errors. No coverage requirement: passing renders is the bar. Examples must render cleanly with no user input and no external services. Dependencies (e.g. BOSL2) must be declared in widget.json but are not auto-installed — consumers must add them to their OpenSCAD library path manually. Importing libraries: use use<> for libraries that only provide modules/functions (no side effects). Use include<> for libraries like BOSL2 that expose constants and special variables — include<> is allowed in src/ for declared dependencies. Standard BOSL2 pattern: include <BOSL2/std.scad> then include <BOSL2/gears.scad> (or whichever submodule). Tests and examples that call your module should use include <../src/your_module.scad> (not use<>) when your src file uses include<> for a library — use<> does not forward include<> statements transitively, so the library constants will be missing at render time. Optional Python sidecar: an openscad widget may carry a python/ directory with stdlib-only calc helpers (printability checks, gear ratios, threading math). Filenames mirror src/ (src/threads.scad ↔ python/threads.py + python/test_threads.py). Sidecars validate at 60% coverage and may not declare dependencies — stdlib only. Delete python/ if not used.
language_notes.systemverilog: No project-specific names, signal names tied to a particular design, or system identifiers in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic RTL names. Use SystemVerilog (.sv) for all files. Testbenches use $fatal(1, "message") to signal failures and $finish to exit cleanly — vvp exits non-zero on $fatal, so it maps directly to test pass/fail. `timescale belongs in testbenches, never in src/. No `initial` blocks, #delays, or $display/$monitor in src/ — these are simulation-only constructs. Vendor primitives (LUT6, BUFG, ALTPLL, etc.) are blocked unless the vendor library is declared in dependencies — generic RTL is the default. Use always_ff for sequential logic, always_comb for combinational — `always @(...)` is blocked; we enforce SystemVerilog idioms. All tunable values (clock frequency, baud rate, data width, address width) must be module parameters with defaults and unit comments. Parameters are the variation points: a consumer should be able to instantiate your module with different parameters without touching source. Reset must be a parameter-defined polarity (active-high or active-low) with synchronous behavior as the default. No hardcoded sizes or widths — everything that varies by use case must be a parameter. $readmemh/$readmemb file paths must be parameters, not hardcoded strings.
language_notes.angular: No project-specific names, identifiers, or terminology anywhere in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic names like 'item', 'value', 'example.com'. A test or component that references your project's real entity names or domain is contaminated. Use Angular standalone components (@Component with standalone: true) - avoid NgModule boilerplate. Use ng test --watch=false for all tests - Karma + Jasmine runs in ChromeHeadlessNoSandbox (configured in karma.conf.js). Coverage threshold is 80% and is enforced via karma.conf.js check.global - do not lower these values. Declare additional npm dependencies in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies as '@scope/package >= version' or 'package >= version'. No console.log() in src/ files. Use named exports, not default exports. No process.exit() in src/. Example validation deviates from standard: examples cannot be executed as scripts - instead, ng build compiles the library and type-checks examples/ via tsconfig.lib.json. The example must compile without TypeScript errors; it does not need to run. URLs and endpoints belong in examples as demonstration data, not in src/ - accept them as @Input() parameters. Angular-specific contamination: component selectors must be generic (lib-item, lib-value) - not project-branded (lib-mycompany-header). Decorator metadata (@Component selector, templateUrl) must not contain project-specific strings.
language_notes.nim: No project-specific names, identifiers, or terminology anywhere in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic names like 'item', 'value', 'exampleUser'. Use std/unittest for all tests (import std/unittest, not bare import unittest). Use func for pure procedures with no side effects — only use proc when side effects are required. Mark all public symbols with * (e.g. func myFunc*(x: int): int). Use camelCase for funcs/procs/variables, PascalCase for types. Prefer stdlib imports with the std/ prefix (e.g. import std/strutils, not import strutils). No echo in src/ files. No quit() or system.quit() in src/ files. No {.importc.} or {.compile.} pragmas — C FFI makes widgets platform-dependent and unvalidatable. No {.global.} pragma — widgets must not use global mutable state. No OS-targeting when defined(windows/linux/posix/etc.) — widgets must validate on all platforms. No cast[seq[T]] in src/ — GC-managed seq casts break GC invariants and are blocked; copy explicitly or use toOpenArrayByte. Avoid bare `except:` — catches Defect and KeyboardInterrupt; use a typed except like `except CatchableError:`. Avoid raw memory primitives (alloc/dealloc/copyMem, cast[ptr ...], ptr UncheckedArray) — prefer GC-managed seq/string; warns if used. A widget_id.nimble file is required at the widget root - it is created by cartograph create and must stay in sync with widget.json dependencies. List nimble package dependencies in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies as 'pkgname >= version'.
language_notes.php: No project-specific names, identifiers, or terminology anywhere in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic names like 'item', 'value', 'example.com'. A test or class that references your project's real entity names or domain is contaminated. Use PHPUnit for all tests - require phpunit/phpunit in composer.json require-dev. Use PHP 8.1+ features (named arguments, enums, fibers, readonly properties). No echo in src/ files - use return values only. No WordPress globals anywhere (wp_*, add_action, add_filter, $wpdb, $post, $wp_query, get_option, register_post_type, etc.) - PHP widgets must be pure PHP with no framework dependency. Coverage is enforced at 80% via PHPUnit --min-coverage - Xdebug or PCOV must be installed. Declare Composer dependencies in widget.json tech_stack.dependencies as 'vendor/package >= version'. A composer.json and phpunit.xml are required at the widget root - created by cartograph create. Namespace all classes under Cartograph\\YourWidget\\. No die() or exit() in src/ files. URLs and endpoints belong in examples as demonstration data, not in src/ - accept them as constructor parameters or method arguments.
language_notes.terraform: No project-specific names, account IDs, or environment identifiers anywhere in src/, tests/, or examples/ - use generic names like 'name', 'environment', 'tags'. Layout: src/ holds the module (main resource files, variables.tf, outputs.tf, versions.tf), tests/ holds at least one root configuration that calls the module with sample inputs to prove external callability, examples/ holds a root configuration showing typical use. Validation is shape-only: terraform validate runs against src/, tests/, and examples/. There is no test runner and no coverage requirement - widgets harden through use. Modules must NOT declare provider blocks or backend blocks in src/ - those belong to the consumer's root configuration. Modules MUST declare required_version and required_providers in src/versions.tf so consumers know the contract. All variation points must be input variables with descriptions and types - never hardcode region, account ID, instance size, or naming prefix. Real AWS account IDs in arn:aws:* strings are blocked - use placeholders (000000000000) or accept as a variable. Hardcoded credentials (access_key, secret_key, password, api_key) are blocked anywhere. terraform init runs with TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR set so providers download once across src/, tests/, and examples/. Provider versions are pinned in versions.tf - widget.json tech_stack.dependencies is not used to pin Terraform providers.

domain_notes.backend: Every tunable should be a parameter: timeouts, retry counts, pool sizes, base URLs, header names. A consumer must be able to point your widget at any endpoint or database without touching source. Never hardcode URLs in src/ - accept them as parameters and demonstrate with a real URL in examples/. Return structured data (dicts, typed objects) rather than formatted strings - let the caller decide how to present it. Do not log to stdout/stderr; raise exceptions or return error values instead.
domain_notes.data: Transformation logic must be pure and stateless - same input always produces same output, no side effects. Accept the broadest practical input type (bytes, str, file-like, path) and let the caller choose. Expose encoding, delimiter, schema, and other format details as parameters. Raise descriptive errors on malformed input rather than silently coercing or dropping data.
domain_notes.ml: Expose model path, endpoint URL, and inference parameters (temperature, max_tokens, thresholds) as arguments - never hardcode them. API base URLs belong in examples/ as demonstration data, not in src/. Return raw model output or a typed result object; do not format or truncate. See language_notes for framework-specific constraints.
domain_notes.security: Never log secrets, tokens, or PII - not even partially. Accept credentials as parameters, never read them from environment variables or files internally. Auth endpoints and redirect URIs must be parameters - never hardcode OAuth URLs, token endpoints, or redirect URIs in src/; put real URLs in examples/ to demonstrate. Crypto parameters (key size, algorithm, salt rounds) must be explicit arguments with safe defaults. Fail closed: on any ambiguous input, reject rather than guess.
domain_notes.infra: Accept all paths and hostnames as parameters - never construct paths from hardcoded roots. Config keys, log formats, and health check endpoints must be configurable. Return structured status objects rather than printing; let the caller handle output. Side effects (file writes, process spawns) must be opt-in, not automatic.
domain_notes.frontend: All appearance values (colors, spacing, typography, shadows) must be exposed as parameters or CSS custom properties - hardcoded values lock consumers into your choices. Provide sensible defaults but every visual value must be overridable. No inline styles for anything that could vary by theme.
domain_notes.universal: Use this domain when a widget spans multiple domains or has no clear home — not because it must be pure. A retry utility, a date formatter, a general-purpose HTTP client all belong here. Expose variation points as parameters. Don't force it into a domain just to avoid universal.
domain_notes.modeling: Every dimension and tolerance must be a parameter with a sensible default - never hardcode sizes. Module names must be nouns describing the shape, not verbs. Include a parameter for fit tolerance where physical assembly is involved. All parameters must have comments explaining units (mm, degrees) and valid ranges. Default units: lengths in millimeters, angles in degrees. Widgets must render cleanly with default parameters - the example must produce a non-empty mesh. Every src/ file must declare a coordinate frame so consumers know how the part is oriented before they instantiate it: pick the system that matches the geometry (cartesian for chassis-like parts, cylindrical for rotational parts like gears or threads, spherical for radial parts like balls/lenses). State the origin and axis meanings concretely (e.g. 'Origin: bottom-back-center of the chair', '+X: forward (away from the seatback)') — generic placeholders are blocked by validation. Right-hand rule applies to all three systems. Examples should use OpenSCAD Customizer annotations (/* [Section] */ blocks with value ranges) so users can adjust parameters interactively in View > Customizer without editing code. Python sidecar (python/) is available for printability/parameter math when the .scad source can't compute something on its own — stdlib-only.
domain_notes.rtl: Every timing constant (clock frequency, baud rate, bit period) and bus width must be a module parameter with a default and a unit comment (// Hz, // bits, // bytes). Never hardcode these — a consumer must be able to instantiate your module at any clock frequency or bus width by changing parameters only. Module names must be nouns or noun phrases describing the hardware function (uart_tx, spi_master, gray_encoder) — not verbs. All parameters must be synthesizable types (int, logic, bit) — no real, string, or event. The example must compile cleanly and simulate to $finish with vvp. Write testbenches to be self-contained: include all required src files via the compile command, assert expected behavior, and terminate with $finish.
domain_notes.devops: Every variation point must be a module input variable with a type and a description - region, account, environment name, instance size, naming prefix, tags, retention. Never hardcode these - a consumer must be able to apply the module to any environment by passing different variables. Modules must not declare `provider` or `backend` blocks - those are the consumer's choice; declare only required_providers in versions.tf. Outputs must expose every identifier a downstream caller would need (resource id, ARN, endpoint, name) so the module composes cleanly. Tags must be a map(string) input with an empty default. Naming should accept a name or prefix variable rather than constructing identifiers from hardcoded literals. Examples and tests must use placeholder values (000000000000 for account IDs, example.com for domains) - real production identifiers must never appear in widget code.
